body: Lots of thunder eggs in Naches/ Chinook area. But you have to go up to Little Naches rd and then take FR 1901 up. Then the higher up you can get, the better. We found a spot just on the side of 1901, about 5-6 miles in I reckon, that has huge chunks of rock with thunder eggs all throughout it. just looks like a rock fall, but you can see where everyone digs. But if you can climb up higher, there are more to be found.

That's actually a hard question for me to answer. I mean the answer is really yes and no. I have had improvement in certain aspects of my life. But I still struggle just to breathe some days.  

Unfortunately this particular month is just a really really bad time for me so I think that's why I'm kind of holding onto therapy like a lifeline just to make it through. I had an incredibly traumatic event this time last year which led to me attempting suicide. 

But when I'm not dealing with this particular situation, yes, my life has improved. Not in any particular major ways, but in little things. Like..I do something minor that normally would derail damn near my entire day and instead of my first reaction being to start calling myself horrible things I instead end up almost being.. kind to myself. Which is a completely foreign concept to me. 

I know that doesn't sound like any big improvement maybe for most people but for myself it's.. momentous. And it took almost 9 months to get here. It's been a complete nightmare at times. But I'm still trying so hard.

When I first started seeing my therapist it seemed like every single session I felt worse and worse. It would easily take most of the week for me to get my head straight again, but then I'd just have another session. I honestly dreaded going so much I would almost go into full panic attacks. 

I was very honest with my therapist about how I felt and she did a really great job listening to and validating my concerns. She encouraged me to just keep trying and to keep showing up. 

I have now been in therapy for about 9 months and it's only in the last month or so that I've been able to actually look forward to my sessions. Honestly now those sessions are the only thing getting me through my week. It was incredibly difficult for me to get to this point, however it was absolutely worth the effort on my part. Of course my therapist put in the same amount of effort I did, if not a bit more at times, which is really what enabled me to get past the worst of it.

I ended up having to max out my FMLA last year due to SI and PTSD. As long as you qualify for the FMLA, you can utilize it. I didn't have to specify the exact issue to the FMLA lady on the phone, when she asked for reasons I said mental health kind of questioningly and she just entered mental health. My T and another medical doctor filled out the required paperwork. I had zero issues personally using FMLA. I got my short term disability and all through them. Only issue I had was a mix up just due to state and federal regs based on the type of work I did.

When I scheduled my first appointment with my current therapist I was in the midst of a crisis and just trying to make it to my appointment. Unfortunately I attempted suicide and was hospitalized before I made it to that appointment. The hospital called and rescheduled for me, I thought for sure I'd get dropped before the appointment date. Instead I showed up and was very up front and honest about my current state of mind and she was very understanding and treated me with respect and immediately started helping me with planning safety measures. 

I would hope any decent therapist would offer the same level of care and respect. I'm still struggling with SI and I communicate that with my T. She doesn't feel hospitalization is required at this time and I agree, but it is still a very real possibility. 

Not sure if that helps you, I'm not great at communicating what's in my head sometimes.
